result.title: Bilateral Evidence Selection and Reasoning for Mammography Vision--Language Models
result.summary: Medical vision--language models (VLMs) often need to identify small, subtle lesions within high-resolution images containing extensive normal anatomy and redundant visual information. Visual-token compression improves efficiency, but preserving salient regions alone can discard the context needed for diagnostic interpretation. This context can extend across images: in bilateral mammography, the opposite breast provides a patient-specific anatomical reference. Yet retaining such evidence does not ensure that the model uses it effectively. We propose Bilateral Evidence Selection and Reasoning (BESR), which connects evidence preservation with comparative assessment through a bilateral-guided token selector and a bilateral reward. Under a shared token budget, the selector jointly prioritizes lesion appearance and its local and bilateral context, while the reward encourages assessments that benefit from the preserved comparison. Experiments on a bilateral dataset constructed from CBIS-DDSM and on VinDr-Mammo demonstrate improved evidence retention and diagnostic performance under constrained visual-token budgets. Inference benchmarking further shows reduced prefill latency.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BESR：在共享 token 预算下用双边引导的 token 选择器同时保留病灶外观及其局部与对侧上下文，并施加双边奖励促使诊断评估真正利用所保留的对比证据，在乳腺钼靶数据集上验证证据保留与诊断表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文明确指出「保留证据不等于模型会使用它」，与视觉证据筛选、视觉旁路及贡献分配的问题直接对应，其选择器与奖励设计可作为 LVR 中按任务必要性筛选视觉细节并检验其因果作用的核查线索。
